text:
maria (support): Hey team, customer (AcmeApps) reports 502s and TLS failures when calling their private service endpoint after a migration to a new account. They say it worked before.

alex (eng-infra): Quick sanity—are they hitting a private DNS name that might be resolving to the wrong ALB/cert?

maria (support): They see this from their app hosts in our VPC: `curl https://svc.acme.internal/api/health` -> `curl: (60) SSL: no alternative certificate subject name matches target host name 'svc.acme.internal'`

kamal (sre): That screams split-horizon / wrong cert. Can you paste dig from a host in their VPC?

maria (support): Asked customer to run: `dig @169.254.169.253 svc.acme.internal A +short` (their VPC resolver) and they returned `10.10.4.22` which is the old staging ALB IP not the new prod target.

jess (solutions): Do we have any cross-account private hosted zone associations for svc.acme.internal? If the old account still has a private hosted zone associated to this VPC that would shadow the new one.

alex (eng-infra): Yup. Likely duplicate private hosted zone. Steps to confirm from our side: 
1) Confirm hosted zones in customer account(s): `aws route53 list-hosted-zones --query 'HostedZones[?Name==\`svc.acme.internal.\`]'`
2) Check VPC associations: `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id ZONEID`

kamal (sre): Also validate resolver rules: `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rules --filters Name=DomainName,Values=svc.acme.internal` in BOTH accounts. I've seen resolver rules silently catch queries and forward to another zone.

maria (support): Customer also ran `openssl s_client -connect 10.10.4.22:443 -servername svc.acme.internal` and got cert subject `CN = staging.alb.internal` so mismatch.

alex (eng-infra): That confirms it. The VPC is getting a record that points to a staging ALB with staging cert. Because Route53 private zone hosted in old account is associated with the VPC, it's authoritative.

jess (solutions): Quick mitigation options: 
- Disassociate the old private zone from the VPC (if safe). 
- Update the old zone's record to point to the new ALB (stopgap). 
- Update resolver rule priorities so the customer's prod zone is preferred.

maria (support): Customer asked if firewall/egress allowlist might cause this — they have NAT egress allowlist that blocks outbound 53 to internet. But these are VPC-internal lookups so should not be affected.

kamal (sre): Good to double-check outbound 53 from app hosts to the VPC resolver IP (UDP 53). If they forced DNS to an external resolver, they may see public resolution which points to a public endpoint with different cert. Run: `dig @169.254.169.253 svc.acme.internal +trace` and `cat /etc/resolv.conf` on one of their app hosts.

maria (support): Customer pasted `/etc/resolv.conf` and it's the VPC resolver address. So internal resolver is used.

alex (eng-infra): Next ask: which hosted zone is associated to the VPC? Run in both accounts: 
```
aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name svc.acme.internal.
# then for each zoneid
aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id ZONEID
```
We should see two zones; one still associated.

jess (solutions): Also check for resolver endpoints/rules that forward to another VPC/account (cross-account resolver). Sometimes we create rules to forward `*.internal` to a partner account.

maria (support): I checked the customer's hosted zones. They have 2 zones: Z1 (prod-new) in acct A and Z2 (staging-old) in acct B. Z2 is still associated with the VPC, so queries are served by staging-old.

kamal (sre): That's the root cause. Suggested fix: disassociate Z2 from the VPC. If they can't remove association immediately (shared infra), use record update in Z2 to point to correct ALB or set an alias to the new ALB.

alex (eng-infra): Operational checklist before disassociate: 
- Confirm no other services rely on Z2 for names in that VPC. 
- Take a Route53 zone export (or snapshot) for rollback. 
- Change DNS TTLs to low for smoother cutover.

maria (support): Customer wants a safe plan. I'll propose: 
1) Lower TTL on conflicting records in Z2 to 30s. 
2) Update A/alias in Z2 to point to new ALB endpoint. 
3) Verify from their app hosts with `dig` and `openssl` that cert matches. 
4) After verification, fully disassociate Z2.

jess (solutions): Also add a monitoring alert for certificate name mismatch in our prod metrics (we have code that parses `curl` failures and flags subject mismatch). Can help detect regressions.

maria (support): Customer implemented the change (updated Z2 aliases to new ALB) and after ~45s their `curl` succeeded. `curl -v` shows `Verified OK` and cert CN `svc.acme.internal`.

alex (eng-infra): Excellent. Please coordinate to remove the stale zone association as next maintenance step. Also recommend they consolidate zones or use resolver rules rather than cross-account zone associations.

kamal (sre): FYI, we should add a runbook for this pattern: "private hosted zone shadowing → TLS mismatch". It's common and noisy.

alerts-bot: Incident INC-2451 created for "Private DNS shadowing caused TLS cert mismatch for svc.acme.internal".

maria (support): I'll file follow-up ticket with the customer to confirm clean disassociation and install runbook link. Closing slack thread but keeping incident open until final disassociate. :eyes:
